Session RPE load

Source: R/descriptors.R
srpe_load.Rd

Computes the session rating of perceived exertion (RPE) load of Foster (1998) and Foster et al. (2001): the RPE of the session multiplied by its duration in minutes (MODELS.md, M-10).

Usage

srpe_load(rpe, duration)

Arguments

rpe

Numeric vector of session RPE values, each between 0 and 10 or NA.

duration

Numeric vector of session durations in minutes, each >= 0 or NA. Must have the same length as rpe, or one of the two must have length 1.

Value

A numeric vector, rpe * duration. NA in either argument gives NA.

Details

$$w = \mathrm{RPE} \times D$$

Collecting the data

  • RPE is rated on the 0-10 category-ratio scale: one global rating for the whole session, asked about 30 minutes after it ends.

  • Duration is the duration in minutes of the entire session, including warm-up, cool-down and recovery intervals.

Several sessions on the same day are summed when the loads are passed to as_daily_load().

Session RPE load is in arbitrary units. Comparing it across athletes needs care.

References

Foster C (1998). Monitoring training in athletes with reference to overtraining syndrome. Medicine and Science in Sports and Exercise, 30(7), 1164-1168.

Foster C, Florhaug JA, Franklin J, et al. (2001). A new approach to monitoring exercise training. Journal of Strength and Conditioning Research, 15(1), 109-115.

See also

as_daily_load() to build the daily series, rolling_load() and monotony_strain() to describe it.

Examples

# The week of Foster (1998), Table 1
srpe_load(rpe = c(5, 7, 2, 6, 7, 2, 7),
          duration = c(180, 120, 20, 90, 75, 20, 120))
#> [1] 900 840  40 540 525  40 840
